<loc_23><loc_174><loc_93><loc_181>Visit Summary:
<loc_22><loc_182><loc_465><loc_278>Jessica Chen, a 28-year-old female, presents for evaluation of a rash that appeared one week ago. It began as a single patch on her flank and has since spread to her back and upper arms. The rash is mildly pruritic, but she denies any pain, fever, or other associated symptoms. She has not changed any detergents, soaps, or lotions recently. The physical examination is notable for a "herald patch" on her right flank and multiple smaller, oval, pink papules with fine scale distributed along cleavage lines on her back, classic for a "Christmas tree" pattern. <loc_25><loc_133><loc_460><loc_149>Clinical History: 28-year-old female with a one-month history of a painless, enlarging left-sided neck mass. Associated with night sweats. Concern for lymphoma.
<loc_25><loc_150><loc_446><loc_166>Diagnosis: Lymph Node, Left Cervical, Excision: Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma, Nodular Sclerosis Type.
<loc_24><loc_168><loc_466><loc_236>Gross Description: Received fresh, labeled 'left neck mass,' is an encapsulated lymph node measuring 2.8 x 2.1 x 1.5 cm. The cut surface is tan-white and firm, with a vaguely nodular appearance. Microscopic Description: Sections of the lymph node show complete effacement of the normal architecture by a nodular infiltrate. The nodules are defined by broad bands of collagenous fibrosis. Within the nodules, there is a mixed inflammatory background composed of small lymphocytes, eosinophils, and histiocytes. Scattered throughout this background are large, atypical cells, including classic binucleated Reed-Sternberg cells and their mononuclear variants (Hodgkin cells). These cells have large, vesicular nuclei, prominent eosinophilic nucleoli, and abundant cytoplasm.
<loc_24><loc_237><loc_406><loc_245>Immunohistochemistry: The large, atypical cells show the following immunophenotype:
<loc_23><loc_246><loc_86><loc_253>CD30: Positive
<loc_23><loc_254><loc_87><loc_261>CD15: Positive
<loc_23><loc_262><loc_110><loc_270>PAX5: Positive (dim)
<loc_23><loc_271><loc_90><loc_278>CD45: Negative
<loc_23><loc_279><loc_90><loc_286>CD20: Negative
<loc_23><loc_288><loc_238><loc_295>CD3: Highlights the background T-cell population.
<loc_22><loc_296><loc_442><loc_321>Comment: The morphologic findings in conjunction with the immunophenotype (CD30+, CD15+, PAX5+, CD45-) are diagnostic of Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma, Nodular Sclerosis subtype. Clinical correlation and appropriate oncologic management are recommended.

<loc_14><loc_188><loc_442><loc_206>Diagnosis: Gastric Antrum, Biopsy: Mild chronic gastritis, positive for Helicobacter pylori. Gross Description: Received in formalain, labeled "gastric antrum," are three tan mucosal fragments,

<loc_38><loc_205><loc_472><loc_253>Light Microscopy Description: The specimen consists of two cores of renal cortex and medulla. Up to 28 glomeruli are identified for evaluation. <loc_38><loc_337><loc_455><loc_363>Electron Microscopy Description: Electron microscopy confirms diffuse subendothelial and mesangial electron-dense deposits. Tubuloreticular inclusions are present within endothelial cells. There is approximately 50% podocyte foot process effacement.

<loc_61><loc_137><loc_480><loc_153>Clinical History: 28-year-old female with a one-month history of a painless, enlarging left-sided neck mass. Associated with night sweats. Concern for lymphoma.
<loc_61><loc_153><loc_470><loc_170>Diagnosis: Lymph Node Left Cenical, Excision: Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma, Nodular Sclerosis Type
<loc_61><loc_170><loc_484><loc_197>Gross Description: Received fresh, labeled 'left neck mass' is an encapsulated lymph node measuring 2.8x2.1x15cm. The cut surface is tan-white and firm, with a vaguely nodular appearance. Microscopic Description Scans of the lymph node show complete effacement of the normal architecture by a nodular microtubule. The nodules are defined by broad bands of collagenous fibrosis.
<loc_61><loc_197><loc_484><loc_242>Within the nodules, there is a mixed inflammatory background composed of small lymphocytes. eosinophils, and histiocytes. Scattered throughout this background are large, atypical cells, including classic binucleated Reed-Sternberg cells and their mononuclear variants (Hodgkin cells). These cells have large, vesicular nuclei, prominent eosinophilic nucleolus, and abundant cytoplasm. Immunohistochemistry: The large, atypical cells show the following immunophenotype:
<loc_57><loc_242><loc_101><loc_250>CD30: Positive
<loc_57><loc_250><loc_101><loc_258>CD15: Positive
<loc_57><loc_258><loc_141><loc_266>PAX5: Positive (dim)
<loc_57><loc_266><loc_141><loc_274>CD45: Negative
<loc_57><loc_274><loc_121><loc_282>CD20: Negative
<loc_57><loc_282><loc_121><loc_290>CD3: Hightlights the background
<loc_57><loc_290><loc_263><loc_298>Comment: The morphologic findings in conjunction with the immunophenotype (CD30+, CD15+,
<loc_57><loc_298><loc_465><loc_316>PAX5+, CD45-) are diagnostic of Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma, Nodular Sclerosis subtype. Clinical correlation and appropriate oncologic management are recommended.
